newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate rises to 14.862 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate rises to 14.862 pct.

text.p: The Philippine 91-day treasury bill yield rose to 14.862 pct from 13.572 last week, the Bureau of Treasury said on Monday.
The 182-day T-bill rose to 15.235 percent from 13.967.
The 364-day T-bill rose to 15.667 percent from 14.416.
The Bureau of Treasury, which had expected to sell two billion pesos worth of T-bills, only accepted 700 million pesos worth out of the total tenders of 1.796 billion pesos.
Total accepted bids for the 91-day bills reached 500 million pesos out of the tenders of 795 million pesos.
The awards for the 182-day bills and 364-day bills amounted to 100 million pesos each with bids at 450 million pesos and 551 million pesos respectively.
National Treasurer Caridad Valdehuesa said the auction results were higher than expected.
"There is probably less liquidity in the market," she said, pointing to the central bank's decision to raise liquidity reserve requirements for banks.
The central bank last week raised reserves on bank deposits and trust funds to prevent currency speculation.
